Confidence would increase with dialog-specific BOW ablations, human evaluation, oracle-vs-predicted-y comparisons, and quantitative probes of z.

consensus_findings: Modeling a discourse-level latent variable with a CVAE-style architecture is a coherent and plausible approach to address one-to-many variation in open-domain dialog; the manuscript presents correct derivations and a clear generative framing (p(x,z|c)=p(x|z,c)p(z|c)).

kgCVAE (conditioning the decoder on explicit linguistic labels y and predicting y from (z,c)) is a well-specified architectural integration that can provide an interface for supervision and potential interpretability/control.

A bag-of-words (BOW) auxiliary loss added to the variational objective (optionally combined with KL-annealing) is a pragmatic optimization technique that increases the KL term and reduces perplexity in the unconditional PTB VAE experiments presented, mitigating KL collapse in that setting.

Under the tested generation protocol (sampling z and greedy decoding for CVAE/kgCVAE versus per-step softmax sampling for the baseline), CVAE and kgCVAE produce higher recall (coverage of retrieved references) and kgCVAE attains higher precision+recall on the reported automatic metrics on Switchboard.

Qualitative analyses (examples and t-SNE) show suggestive patterns that the posterior z correlates with dialog-act labels and response length, indicating potential interpretability of the learned latent space.
disagreements: Degree of empirical support for transfer of BOW optimization benefits from PTB LM to the conditional dialog CVAE: several reviewers note convincing PTB ablation but disagree about sufficiency of dialog-specific ablation evidence—some view the transfer claim as plausible but under-documented; others treat the lack of conditional ablation as a major gap.

Reliability of the automated multi-reference evaluation pipeline: reviewers agree it is a useful pragmatic approach but disagree on how much the reported precision/recall numbers can be trusted given that the reference classifier has only ~71% CV accuracy; some reviewers treat this as a central flaw, others as an uncertainty mitigated by other metrics and qualitative examples.

Interpretability strength of z (clusters by dialog act/length): reviewers accept qualitative correlation but disagree about whether t-SNE alone suffices—some expect quantitative cluster/probing evidence to back the interpretability claim, others see the qualitative evidence as reasonable preliminary support.

Sufficiency of decoding baselines: reviewers concur that comparisons are limited (baseline softmax sampling only) but differ on how critical this omission is to the paper's core claims—some consider it a moderate methodological limitation, others see it as a major missing control.
uncertainty_hotspots: Multi-reference construction and filtering: retrieval + human-filter on 240 samples + trained classifier (71% CV acc) was used to expand references. The precision/recall metrics depend critically on this pipeline's quality and calibration.
Dialog-act supervision quality: kgCVAE uses dialog-act labels largely produced by an SVM with ~77% held-out accuracy. Noise in y affects both training of kgCVAE and dialog-act-match evaluation.

Transfer of BOW results: main preventive evidence against KL collapse comes from PTB unconditional VAE experiments; whether BOW yields the same non-trivial KL and generation-quality gains in conditional dialog CVAE requires explicit ablation and training-curve evidence on Switchboard.

Interpretation of KL magnitude: KL increase is used as a proxy for meaningful latent utilization; without targeted probes or controlled manipulations of z, KL changes are ambiguous (useful signal vs encoding superficial statistics or overfitting).

Decoding regime scope: claims that sampling z + greedy decoding 'suffices' are supported only relative to the tested baseline (per-step softmax sampling). Performance under other common decoding strategies (beam, temperature/top-k/top-p, diverse beam) is untested.

Generality across datasets/architectures: experiments presented are Switchboard (dialog) and PTB (LM ablation); robustness to other dialog corpora, differently sized models, or different recognition/prior architectures is not evaluated.
model_diversity_effects: The experimental setup isolates discourse-level variation by sampling z and decoding greedily, and under that regime CVAE/kgCVAE increase recall (i.e., match more retrieved plausible references) relative to a baseline that introduces noise at token level via per-step softmax sampling; this suggests the latent can produce qualitatively different intents rather than only lexical noise.

However, because the baseline decoding strategies are narrow, part of the measured diversity advantage may reflect that the sampled-z + greedy configuration shifts randomness to a different part of the generation pipeline; alternative decoding methods for the baseline might reduce or change the observed gap.

kgCVAE's conditioning on y appears to increase precision while retaining diversity, indicating that auxiliary linguistic supervision can regularize latent-driven diversity toward more coherent responses—subject to the caveat that noisy y may both help and bias outputs.

BOW auxiliary loss appears to change training dynamics (larger KL, lower perplexity) enabling the latent to be non-trivially used; whether the additional diversity produced is semantically meaningful (intent-level) rather than surface-level bag statistics remains to be demonstrated via probes and human judgment.
meta_review.editor_guidance: Treat the manuscript as a methodologically coherent, incremental contribution that proposes pragmatic solutions (kgCVAE and BOW loss) to address discourse-level diversity and the vanishing-latent problem. The central technical ideas are sound and experiments are promising, but several methodological and evaluation gaps leave empirical claims partially under-supported. Key checks for authors before strong external claims: (1) provide dialog-specific ablations showing BOW (and KL-annealing) effects on CVAE/kgCVAE training curves (KL term, reconstruction loss/perplexity) and downstream generation metrics; (2) validate the automated multi-reference expansion by releasing the retrieved candidate sets, classifier artifacts, and reporting classifier calibration/precision-recall against a larger human-labeled holdout; (3) include human evaluation (appropriateness/diversity) on model outputs to triangulate automatic metrics; (4) add ablations that compare oracle-y vs predicted-y and measure kgCVAE sensitivity to label noise; (5) expand decoding baselines (beam, nucleus/top-k/temperature) to ensure claimed sufficiency of sampling z + greedy is not an artifact of decoder sampling choices. If the authors supply these additional analyses and data, the work would be a well-grounded, practically useful empirical contribution. If not, interpret empirical claims (scope/size of gains and interpretability) with caution.
meta_review.author_guidance: To reduce key uncertainties and strengthen attribution of effects, please provide the following targeted additions: (1) Dialog-specific ablation: train CVAE/kgCVAE variants on Switchboard with (a) no BOW/no KLA, (b) KLA only, (c) BOW only, (d) BOW+KLA; report KL term evolution, reconstruction/perplexity, and the same precision/recall metrics for each variant. (2) Reference-pipeline transparency and validation: release retrieved candidate lists, the training/validation splits of the 240 human-labeled pairs, the trained reference-classifier model (or at minimum confusion matrices, ROC/PR curves), and a sensitivity analysis showing how precision/recall change with classifier thresholds and reference-set sizes. (3) Human evaluation: conduct a blind human annotation (crowd or expert) on a stratified sample of contexts comparing baseline, CVAE, and kgCVAE across appropriateness and perceived diversity; report inter-annotator agreement and link results to automatic metrics. (4) kgCVAE label-ablation: evaluate kgCVAE trained on gold-labelled subset and compare inference conditioning with oracle-y vs predicted-y; also analyze per-class dialog-act confusion and how that maps to generation errors. (5) Decoding baselines: add experiments using beam search, temperature/top-k/top-p sampling, and diverse beam search for the baseline (and optionally for CVAE/kgCVAE) to test robustness of the sampling-z + greedy claim. (6) Interpretability probes: compute quantitative cluster metrics (purity, NMI, ARI) between z clusters and dialog-act/length labels, and train simple probes (e.g., logistic regression) to predict y from z. (7) Release code, seeds, and model checkpoints for reproducibility, including the BOW loss implementation and KL annealing schedule. Addressing these will materially reduce epistemic uncertainty and strengthen the evidence chain behind the main claims.
transparency_report: Provided artifacts in manuscript: model architectures, objective derivations (Eq.4, Eq.6), training hyperparameters (embedding sizes, optimizer), PTB LM ablation table (KL and perplexity), and Appendix A describing the retrieval + human-filter + classifier pipeline for multi-reference expansion.

Missing or partially-documented artifacts that impair reproducibility: trained reference-classifier parameters and evaluation stats (confusion matrix, ROC/PR), the retrieved candidate-reference lists, dialog-act SVM model and per-class confusion matrix, full dialog-specific ablation logs (KL evolution, reconstruction loss) for CVAE/kgCVAE variants, random seeds and checkpoint selection criteria, and code for the BOW auxiliary loss and generation scripts (sampling z + greedy).

Recommended transparency actions: publish (a) code and scripts to reproduce training and evaluation, (b) expanded multi-reference sets and the classifier used to label them (or at least held-out human-labeled validation), (c) dialog-act labeller and its performance breakdown, (d) logs/plots of ELBO decomposition (KL and reconstruction terms) over training for each reported condition, and (e) sampled generations used for reported metrics with IDs linking to the multi-reference sets.
epistemic_limits: The synthesis relies on the manuscript's reported experiments and reviewers' assessments; limitations include: (1) all reviewers saw the same provided experimental summaries rather than raw training logs or full datasets, so judgments about effect sizes and robustness are constrained by what was reported; (2) the automated multi-reference and dialog-act labelling pipelines introduce uncertainty that propagates into many quantitative claims—this synthesis cannot re-evaluate or correct those pipelines without access to the artifacts or human-validated subsets; (3) PTB LM results convincingly show BOW helps in unconditional VAE training, but extrapolation to conditional dialog CVAE remains inferential until dialog-specific ablations are provided; (4) t-SNE visualizations and KL magnitudes are suggestive but not definitive evidence of semantic/discourse encoding in z—the synthesis therefore treats interpretability claims as provisional pending quantitative probes and human assessments; (5) absence of comparisons to wider decoding baselines means claims about sufficiency of sampling z + greedy are conditional on the tested baseline and decoding regime. These epistemic constraints imply that the presented conclusions are best read as promising, hypothesis-supporting evidence rather than conclusive demonstrations of generality.

human_facing_meta_review.summary: The paper adapts conditional variational autoencoders (CVAE) to open-domain dialog by (1) introducing a discourse-level latent z, (2) proposing kgCVAE that conditions on and predicts linguistic features y (dialog acts), and (3) adding a bag-of-words (BOW) auxiliary loss (optionally with KL annealing) to mitigate vanishing-latent issues. Experiments on Switchboard report higher recall (diversity) for CVAE/kgCVAE versus an encoder-decoder baseline under a sampled-z + greedy decoding protocol; kgCVAE further improves precision and yields interpretable predicted dialog-act labels. PTB language-model ablations show BOW (+KLA) produces substantially larger KL and lower perplexity, supporting the optimization claim. Qualitative t-SNE visualizations suggest z correlates with dialog acts and length. However, several evaluation and ablation gaps introduce important uncertainties about generality and attribution of effects.
strengths: Clear probabilistic framing: p(x,z|c)=p(x|z,c)p(z|c) linking the one-to-many dialog problem to a conditional latent model (Sections 3.1, Introduction).
Practical optimization contribution: bag-of-words (BOW) auxiliary loss is well-motivated and empirically increases KL and reduces perplexity on PTB VAE ablations (Section 3.3; Table 3, Section 5.4).

Architectural integration of linguistic priors: kgCVAE explicitly predicts/conditions on dialog-act labels y, providing a concrete interface for supervision and potential interpretability/control (Section 3.2).

Multi-metric evaluation design that attempts to measure discourse-level coverage and appropriateness via generalized precision/recall with BLEU, bag-of-words embedding measures, and dialog-act match (Section 5.2).
limitations: Primary evaluation depends on an automatically-expanded multi-reference set produced by IR + small human filtering + a classifier (described in Appendix A) whose cross-validated accuracy is modest (~71%). Precision/recall results hinge on this pipeline and can be biased by retrieval/classification errors.

Key optimization ablation supporting the BOW claim is performed on Penn Treebank (unconditional VAE). Direct, fully-detailed ablations of BOW and KL-annealing in the conditional dialog CVAE/kgCVAE training (Switchboard) are insufficiently reported to verify transfer of effects.

kgCVAE relies heavily on dialog-act labels produced by an SVM with ~77.3% held-out accuracy (Section 4.1). Label noise both in supervision and in the dialog-act-match evaluation metric is a confounder that is not fully disentangled (no oracle-y vs predicted-y ablation).

Comparative generation baselines are narrow: the main comparison is encoder-decoder with per-step softmax sampling versus sampled-z + greedy decoding for CVAE/kgCVAE. Other common decoding strategies (beam search, temperature/top-k/top-p, diverse beam) and alternative latent/dialog baselines are not reported, limiting the generality of the 'sampling-z suffices' claim.
open_questions: Please provide dialog-specific ablations: how do CVAE/kgCVAE behave on Switchboard when trained with (a) no BOW/no KLA, (b) KLA only, (c) BOW only, and (d) BOW+KLA? Report KL evolution, reconstruction loss/perplexity, and the same precision/recall metrics for each.

Can the authors release (or summarize) the retrieved candidate lists and the trained reference-classifier artifacts (confusion matrix, PR/ROC curves) used to construct the multi-reference sets? How sensitive are precision/recall results to classifier thresholds and to human-validated subsets?

How does kgCVAE perform when conditioned on oracle (human) dialog-act labels at test time compared to predicted-y? Provide ablations showing performance differences and analysis of how label noise affects generation quality.

Have the authors compared baseline and proposed models across alternative decoding strategies (beam search, nucleus/top-k, temperature annealing, diverse beam)? If so, please report precision/recall and human-evaluation comparisons under matched decoding budgets.

Can the authors quantify interpretability beyond t-SNE? e.g., classifier accuracy predicting dialog-act from posterior z, cluster purity/NMI, or controlled latent swaps/interpolations showing predictable changes in dialog-act or response attributes.

Does the increased KL under BOW(+KLA) correspond to semantically useful/discourse-level information rather than surface bag statistics? Please provide probing analyses or human judgments linking KL increases to downstream controllable behavior.
consensus_snapshot: CVAE-style discourse-level latent is a coherent approach to model one-to-many dialog variation; derivations and implementation details are sound and well-described (Sections 3.1-3.3).
kgCVAE is a plausible mechanism to inject linguistic priors via predicted dialog-act labels into latent learning and decoding, enabling interpretable outputs.

BOW auxiliary loss is an effective practical technique for preventing KL collapse in the reported PTB LM experiments; combining BOW with KL annealing yields substantially larger KL and lower perplexity (Table 3).

Under the paper's sampled-z + greedy decoding generation protocol, CVAE and kgCVAE increase recall relative to the presented baseline; kgCVAE tends to improve precision as well on the automatic metrics.
disagreement_snapshot: Whether the PTB BOW ablation convincingly transfers to the conditional dialog CVAE setting: some reviewers find PTB evidence compelling and accept transfer as plausible; others require explicit Switchboard ablations and training-curve evidence before accepting the claim.

How trustworthy the precision/recall gains are given the automatically-expanded multi-reference set: reviewers agree the approach is useful but disagree about the magnitude of its impact on reported results—some treat the 71% classifier accuracy as a major flaw, others as an uncertainty that can be addressed with additional validation.

Sufficiency of decoding baselines: a subset of reviewers consider the lack of comparisons to beam/nucleus/top-k a moderate omission; some consider it a major limitation that could change interpretation of the sampling-z claim.
uncertainty_snapshot: The multi-reference expansion classifier (Appendix A) has limited validation (240 human labels, ~71% CV accuracy). This injects epistemic uncertainty into all recall/precision-based claims.
Dialog-act labels (SVM ~77% accuracy) used to train and evaluate kgCVAE are noisy; observed kgCVAE gains may be sensitive to label quality.

KL magnitude is treated as a proxy for latent utilization. Without probes or controlled latent manipulations, increased KL is ambiguous: it could reflect useful discourse encoding or superficial bag-of-words/statistical memorization.
Generality across datasets, decoders, and architectures is unproven: experiments are limited to Switchboard and PTB (for ablation), and to one decoding regimen for primary comparisons.
source_trace: Appendix A (multi-reference retrieval and classifier pipeline): retrieval of 10 neighbors per context, human-filtering on 240 pairs, classifier trained (71% CV accuracy) to label remaining candidates; reported average ~6.69 references per context (Appendix A).
Section 3.3 and Equation 6: derivation and incorporation of bag-of-words (BOW) auxiliary loss into variational lower bound (Section 3.3).
Table 3 and Section 5.4: Penn Treebank VAE LM ablation results showing Perplexity and KL for Standard, KLA, BOW, BOW+KLA (Table 3; Section 5.4 discussion).
Section 3.2 and Eq.4: kgCVAE objective modification adding log p(y|z,c) and conditioning decoder on predicted y (Section 3.2).
Section 5.2 and Figure 4: reported precision/recall results and higher recall for CVAE/kgCVAE versus baseline under sampled-z + greedy decoding (Section 5.2; Figure 4).
Section 5.3 and Figure 5: t-SNE visualization of posterior z colored by top dialog-act labels and discussion of correlations with dialog act and length (Section 5.3; Figure 5).

transparency_notes: Manuscript provides architecture descriptions, objective derivations (Eq.4, Eq.6), hyperparameters (Section 4.2), PTB ablation table (Table 3), and Appendix A describing multi-reference construction. Missing reproducibility artifacts: trained reference-classifier model and evaluation metrics (confusion matrices, PR/ROC), the retrieved candidate/reference lists, dialog-act SVM model and per-class errors, full training logs and ELBO decomposition traces for dialog CVAE/kgCVAE variants, random seeds and checkpoint selection rules, and code for BOW loss and generation scripts. Publishing these (or at least structured summaries/plots and held-out human-validated subsets) would materially increase reproducibility and reduce epistemic uncertainty.

Before elevating strong empirical claims, require additional validation and transparency: (1) dialog-specific ablations for BOW/KLA on CVAE/kgCVAE with KL and reconstruction curves; (2) release or provide calibration/validation of the multi-reference pipeline (retrieved lists and classifier metrics) and run human evaluation to corroborate automatic precision/recall; (3) oracle-vs-predicted-y ablations for kgCVAE to disentangle supervision effects; (4) experiments comparing decoding strategies (beam, nucleus, temperature/top-k) to test robustness of sampling-z + greedy claim; (5) quantitative probes of latent interpretability (predictive probes, cluster purity, latent swaps). If authors supply these analyses and artifacts, the work will represent a useful, practically oriented advance.
human_facing_meta_review.author_guidance: To strengthen evidence and reduce uncertainty, please (1) provide Switchboard-specific ablations isolating BOW and KLA effects (no-BOW/KLA, KLA-only, BOW-only, BOW+KLA) with KL evolution and reconstruction/perplexity curves and downstream precision/recall metrics; (2) publish the retrieved candidate lists, the 240 human-labeled filtering set, and the trained reference-classifier or at least its confusion matrix and PR/ROC curves plus sensitivity analyses over thresholds; (3) run a blind human evaluation (appropriateness and perceived diversity) on a stratified sample of contexts comparing baseline, CVAE, and kgCVAE and report inter-annotator agreement; (4) run kgCVAE oracle-y vs predicted-y tests on the human-labeled subset to quantify how much benefit derives from clean labels; (5) evaluate baseline and proposed models with beam search and nucleus/top-k/temperature sampling to ensure robustness of the sampling-z + greedy claim; (6) add quantitative interpretability probes: train simple classifiers predicting dialog-act/length from z and report accuracy, compute cluster purity/NMI/ARI, and perform controlled z swaps/interpolations to show predictable changes in generated outputs; (7) release code, random seeds, model checkpoints, and BOW/KLA schedule details to facilitate reproduction.
human_facing_meta_review.comments:
Summary:
The manuscript adapts CVAE to dialog by introducing a discourse-level latent z, augments it with a knowledge-guided variant kgCVAE that predicts/conditions on dialog-act labels y, and proposes a bag-of-words auxiliary loss (with optional KL annealing) to avoid vanishing-latent problems. Experiments on Switchboard indicate higher recall (diversity) for CVAE/kgCVAE under sampled-z + greedy decoding and improved precision for kgCVAE; PTB LM ablations show BOW(+KLA) increases KL and lowers perplexity. Qualitative t-SNE and examples suggest z correlates with dialog acts and length.

Strengths:
- Coherent generative framing and clear model derivations (Sections 3.1-3.3).
- Pragmatic optimization trick (BOW) with strong PTB ablation evidence (Table 3) that addresses a known failure mode.
- kgCVAE provides an operational mechanism to inject linguistic priors and produce interpretable predicted labels at test time.
- Evaluation design attempts to measure coverage and appropriateness via multi-metric precision/recall.

Limitations:
- The primary precision/recall evaluation depends on an automatically-expanded multi-reference set using an IR + classifier pipeline with limited validation (Appendix A; classifier CV accuracy ~71%). This raises concern about metric reliability and possible biases in reported gains.
- BOW optimization evidence is strong on PTB (unconditional VAE) but direct dialog-specific ablations (CVAE/kgCVAE on Switchboard) isolating BOW vs KLA effects are not fully presented; transfer is asserted but under-documented.
- kgCVAE training and dialog-act-match evaluation rely on automatic dialog-act labels from an SVM (~77.3% accuracy), introducing label-noise confounds that could alter training dynamics and evaluation outcomes.
- Decoding comparisons are narrow (baseline per-step softmax sampling only); absence of beam/temperature/nucleus/top-k comparisons limits claims that sampling z + greedy 'suffices.'

Open Questions:
1) Provide full Switchboard ablations for BOW/KLA on CVAE/kgCVAE (KL curves, perplexity, precision/recall). 2) Release or summarize multi-reference retrieval results and classifier calibration (confusion matrix, PR/ROC) and show sensitivity of metrics to classifier thresholds. 3) Report kgCVAE oracle-y vs predicted-y generation results on the human-labeled subset to separate supervision benefits from label-noise effects. 4) Compare models under beam search and nucleus/top-k/temperature sampling to test robustness of the sampling-z + greedy claim. 5) Quantify interpretability: classifier accuracy predicting dialog act from z, cluster purity/NMI, and controlled latent manipulations showing predictable changes. 6) Show that increased KL corresponds to semantically useful latent information (probing/ human judgments).

Transparency:
The paper documents architectures, objectives (Eq.4, Eq.6), hyperparameters and PTB ablations (Table 3), and describes the multi-reference pipeline (Appendix A). Missing are released artifacts: retrieved candidate/reference lists, trained reference-classifier and dialog-act SVM models with confusion matrices, dialog-specific training logs (ELBO/KL/reconstruction components), random seeds, and code for BOW loss and generation scripts. Publishing these would materially improve reproducibility and allow independent validation of the precision/recall claims.

confidence_interval.rationale: Upper bound reflects consistent internal evidence: sound model derivation, PTB ablations showing BOW effects, and Switchboard metrics indicating recall/precision gains under the tested regime. Lower bound reflects significant epistemic uncertainties introduced by (1) the automated multi-reference construction with modest classifier accuracy (~71%), (2) noisy dialog-act supervision (~77% SVM accuracy), (3) limited dialog-specific ablations for BOW, and (4) narrow decoding baseline comparisons. Confidence would increase substantially if authors provide the requested ablations, release evaluation artifacts, and run human evaluations and decoding-baseline experiments.

Traditionally, the negation word is determined from a small hand- 727 Kiritchenko, Zhu, & Mohammad crafted list (Taboada et al., 2011). The scope of negation is often assumed to begin from the word following the negation word until the next punctuation mark or the end of the sentence (Polanyi & Zaenen, 2004; Kennedy & Inkpen, 2005). More sophisticated methods to detect the scope of negation through semantic parsing have also been proposed (Li, Zhou, Wang, & Zhu, 2010). A common way to capture the impact of negation is to reverse the polarities of the sentiment words in the scope of negation. Taboada et al. (2011) proposed to shift the sentiment score of a term in a negated context towards the opposite polarity by a ﬁxed amount. However, in their experiments the shift-score model did not agree with human judgment in many cases, especially for negated negative terms. More complex approaches, such as recursive deep models, address negation through semantic composition (Socher, Huval, Manning, & Ng, 2012; Socher et al., 2013). Traditionally, the negation word is determined from a small hand- 727 Kiritchenko, Zhu, & Mohammad crafted list (Taboada et al., 2011). The scope of negation is often assumed to begin from the word following the negation word until the next punctuation mark or the end of the sentence (Polanyi & Zaenen, 2004; Kennedy & Inkpen, 2005). More sophisticated methods to detect the scope of negation through semantic parsing have also been proposed (Li, Zhou, Wang, & Zhu, 2010). A common way to capture the impact of negation is to reverse the polarities of the sentiment words in the scope of negation. Taboada et al. (2011) proposed to shift the sentiment score of a term in a negated context towards the opposite polarity by a ﬁxed amount. However, in their experiments the shift-score model did not agree with human judgment in many cases, especially for negated negative terms. More complex approaches, such as recursive deep models, address negation through semantic composition (Socher, Huval, Manning, & Ng, 2012; Socher et al., 2013).
